findings.text: The MSI capability anchors its message control at byte offset 2, with the remaining capability flag byte at offset 3. Enable is bit 0 value 0x1, available queue depth is bits 1 to 3 mask 0xE, configured queue size is bits 4 to 6 mask 0x70, 64-bit address permission is bit 7 value 0x80, and per-vector masking capability is bit 8 value 0x100.

MSI addressing and payload layout shifts with address width. Lower address is at offset 4 and upper address at offset 8 when 64-bit is permitted. For 32-bit endpoints data is at offset 8, mask at 12 and pending at 16; for 64-bit endpoints data moves to 12, mask to 16 and pending to 20, preserving a 16-bit data item followed by mask then pending words.

MSI-X message control is at offset 2 with table size mask 0x7FF, mask-all bit 0x4000 and enable bit 0x8000. Table pointer is at offset 4 and pending-bit-array pointer at offset 8; each pointer encodes a BAR index in low 3 bits mask 0x7 and a BAR offset in upper bits mask 0xFFFFFFF8. A deprecated BIR mask aliases the PBA BIR value, and the capability register block size is 12 bytes.

Each MSI-X table entry occupies 16 bytes: message lower address at entry offset 0, upper address at 4, message data at 8, and vector control at 12. Within vector control the mask bit is bit 0 value 0x1 and the steering tag occupies the upper half with mask 0xFFFF0000.

The CompactPCI hot-swap control and status register is at offset 2. Device hiding arm is 0x01, ENUM signal mask is 0x02, pending insert-or-extract is 0x04, LED state is 0x08, programming interface field is mask 0x30, extraction status is 0x40 and insertion status is 0x80.

The Advanced Features capability uses length at offset 2, capability byte at 3, control at 4 and status at 5, with total register size 6. Capability advertises transaction-pending bit 0x01 and reset capability bit 0x02; control carries reset initiation bit 0x01; status reports transaction pending bit 0x01.

Enhanced Allocation header reports entry count at offset 2 masked by 0x3F, first entry offset at 4 generally and at 8 for bridges. Each entry header encodes size in low 3 bits and BAR-equivalent indicator in bits 4 to 7 mask 0xF0. Secondary bus mask is 0xFF, subordinate bus mask is 0xFF00 with shift 8. Indicators run 0 for BAR0 through 5 for BAR5, 6 for behind bridge, 7 for not indicated, 8 for expansion ROM, 9 through 14 for virtual-function BAR0 through BAR5, and 15 reserved treated as not indicated.

Each Enhanced Allocation entry carries primary properties mask 0xFF00 and secondary properties mask 0xFF0000. Property codes are 0 non-prefetch memory, 1 prefetch memory, 2 I/O, 3 virtual-function prefetch memory, 4 virtual-function non-prefetch memory, 5 bridge non-prefetch memory, 6 bridge prefetch memory, 7 bridge I/O, 0xFD reserved memory, 0xFE reserved I/O and 0xFF unavailable. Entry flags include writable bit 0x40000000 and enable bit 0x80000000. Base address is at entry offset 4 and maximum offset length at 8; base and limit words use 64-bit indicator bit 0x2 and address mask 0xFFFFFFFC.

PCI-X mode register is at offset 2. Data parity recovery enable is 0x1 and relaxed ordering enable is 0x2. Maximum read byte-count field mask 0xC encodes 512 bytes as 0, 1K as 0x4, 2K as 0x8 and 4K as 0xC. Outstanding split-transaction field mask 0x70 encodes maxima 1 as 0, 2 as 0x10, 3 as 0x20, 4 as 0x30, 8 as 0x40, 12 as 0x50, 16 as 0x60 and 32 as 0x70. Capability version is extracted from bits 12 to 13.

PCI-X status is a 32-bit word at offset 4. It copies device function mask 0xFF and bus number mask 0xFF00, then reports 64-bit 0x10000, 133 MHz 0x20000, discarded split 0x40000, unexpected split 0x80000, complexity 0x100000, designed max read 0x600000, designed max splits 0x3800000, designed max cumulative 0x1C000000, split error 0x20000000, 266 MHz 0x40000000 and 533 MHz 0x80000000. ECC control and status is at offset 8. Block sizes are 8 bytes for version 0 and 24 bytes for versions 1 and 2, with version 2 aliasing version 1.

PCI-X bridge secondary status is at offset 2 with 64-bit secondary 0x1, 133 MHz 0x2, frequency and mode field mask 0x3C0, version field mask 0x3000 where 0x1000 denotes mode 2 only and 0x2000 denotes mode 1 presence, plus 266 MHz 0x4000 and 533 MHz 0x8000; bridge status follows at offset 4. PCI bridge subsystem vendor identifier is at offset 4 and subsystem device identifier at offset 6.

PCI Express capability register is at offset 2 with version mask 0xF, device or port type mask 0xF0, slot-implemented bit 0x100, interrupt message number mask 0x3E00 and flit-mode bit 0x8000. Type codes are 0 endpoint, 1 legacy endpoint, 4 root port, 5 upstream, 6 downstream, 7 PCIe-to-PCI bridge, 8 PCI-to-PCIe bridge, 9 root-complex endpoint and 0xA event collector. Device capabilities at offset 4 encode payload mask 0x7, phantom mask 0x18, extended tag 0x20, L0s latency 0x1C0, L1 latency 0xE00, attention button 0x1000, attention indicator 0x2000, power indicator 0x4000, role-based error reporting 0x8000, slot power value 0x3FC0000, slot power scale 0xC000000, function reset 0x10000000 and TEE I/O 0x40000000.

Device control at offset 8 enables correctable 0x1, non-fatal 0x2, fatal 0x4 and unsupported-request 0x8 reporting, relaxed ordering 0x10, extended tag 0x100, phantom 0x200, auxiliary power 0x400 and no-snoop 0x800, with bridge-retry or reset bit 0x8000. Payload field mask 0xE0 selects 128 bytes 0, 256 bytes 0x20, 512 bytes 0x40, 1024 bytes 0x60, 2048 bytes 0x80 and 4096 bytes 0xA0; read-request field mask 0x7000 selects 128 bytes 0 through 4096 bytes 0x5000 in 0x1000 steps. Device status at offset 0xA reports correctable 0x1, non-fatal 0x2, fatal 0x4, unsupported 0x8, auxiliary power 0x10 and transactions pending 0x20. Version 1 root-complex endpoints without link end at size 12.

Link capabilities at offset 0xC encode maximum speed mask 0xF with values 1 for 2.5, 2 for 5, 3 for 8, 4 for 16, 5 for 32 and 6 for 64 gigatransfers, width mask 0x3F0, ASPM support 0xC00 with L0s 0x400 and L1 0x800, L0s exit 0x7000, L1 exit 0x38000, clock power 0x40000, surprise-down 0x80000, link-active reporting 0x100000, bandwidth notification 0x200000 and port number in the top byte. Link control at 0x10 covers ASPM mask 0x3 with L0s 0x1 and L1 0x2, read boundary 0x8, disable 0x10, retrain 0x20, common clock 0x40, extended sync 0x80, clock request 0x100, autonomous width disable 0x200 and bandwidth interrupts 0x400 and 0x800.

Link status at offset 0x12 reports current speed mask 0xF with values 1 through 6 for 2.5 to 64 gigatransfers, negotiated width mask 0x3F0 with x1 0x10 x2 0x20 x4 0x40 x8 0x80 starting at bit 4, plus training 0x800, slot clock 0x1000, link active 0x2000 and bandwidth management 0x4000 and autonomous 0x8000 states. Version 1 endpoints with link end at size 20.

Slot capabilities at offset 0x14 report attention button 0x1, power controller 0x2, MRL sensor 0x4, attention indicator 0x8, power indicator 0x10, surprise hot-plug 0x20, hot-plug capable 0x40, power limit value 0x7F80, power limit scale 0x18000, interlock 0x20000, no-command-completed 0x40000 and physical slot number in upper bits. Slot control at 0x18 begins with attention-pressed enable 0x1, power-fault enable 0x2, MRL-changed enable 0x4 and presence-changed enable 0x8.

Register geometry is width sensitive: MSI 64-bit permission shifts data, mask and pending words by four bytes relative to 32-bit layout; MSI-X table and pending array pointers always split into a 3-bit BAR selector plus an aligned offset; Enhanced Allocation base and limit words share one address mask with a separate 64-bit flag; PCI-X version 2 reuses version 1 size; PCIe version 1 endpoint length is 12 without link and 20 with link.
